title: Predictive stream cushioning and KV cooperation — exploratory notes
content:
Goal:
Explore a different framing for prefill vs decode concurrency that treats the decode stream as a soft-real-time consumer and the prefill stage as a background producer whose output (KV shards/prefixes) can be "cushioned" to absorb jitter and prioritization decisions.

High-level idea:
- Introduce a per-connection "cushion budget" measured in tokens and latency headroom. Prefill work that populates KV or precomputed prefixes earns credits that are banked on the connection as a cushion.
- Decode phases draw down cushion credits when they would otherwise block waiting on a prefetched KV slot. When cushion is exhausted, the runtime falls back to on-the-fly prefill or to a degraded, lower-cost model variant.
- Cushioning lets us smooth microbatching spikes and favor higher-priority streams without aggressive preemption of longer-running prefill tasks.

Why this is different:
- Most existing notes treat prefill and decode as two phases to arbitrarily overlap or serialize. This doc models them as producer/consumer with a resource abstraction (cushion budget) that both stages respect.
- Allows simple priority-weighted admission and a fair sharing policy across heterogeneous SLAs.

Key components and primitives:
1) Cushion ledger (per-stream, lightweight):
   - tokens_reserved: integer (initially 0) — number of precomputed tokens cached/available for low-latency emit without additional compute.
   - latency_headroom_ms: integer — how much extra latency we can tolerate before breaching SLO.
   - credit_score: derived (tokens_reserved * weight + headroom_ms / scale) — used for scheduling decisions.

2) Prefill policy functions:
   - proactive_prefill(stream_id, predicted_len): try to precompute up to min(predicted_len, max_cushion_per_stream).
   - opportunistic_topup(on_idle_gpu): when GPU is underutilized, topup cushions for nearby streams (region/tenant affinity).

3) Decode admission and draw-down:
   - decode_request(stream_id): if tokens_reserved > 0 -> emit from cushion (decrement).
   - else if credit_score >= threshold -> trigger urgent prefill microbatch (fast path using hot kernels).
   - else -> fast fallback (quantized model variant or synchronous prefill with reduced batch coalescing).

KV cooperation protocol (KV-COOP):
- Purpose: avoid redundant prefill/evict thrash when many concurrent streams share similar prefixes (e.g., multi-turn assistants).
- Shard-level lending: nodes can lend KV slices to nearby workers for a short epoch (t_lend_ms). Lender marks shard as "soft-evictable" but retains a handshake tag.
- Borrower increments cushion tokens for the borrower stream proportional to borrowed KV size.
- Upon borrower completion or timeout, borrower either returns or commits the shard as cold (evictable).

Example flow (user asks long prompt):
- initial request queued -> scheduler predicts 2k decode tokens and 1k prefill tokens needed.
- proactive_prefill tops up 800 tokens into cushion using opportunistic GPU cycles. tokens_reserved=800.
- decode begins, draws 400 tokens immediately from cushion; remaining 600 expected to be filled by background prefill.
- a higher-priority chat arrives -> credit_score comparison shows latter has stronger headroom, scheduler reassigns one topup slot to high-priority tenant; low-priority stream will use fallback after cushion drains.

Heuristics and knobs to tune:
- max_cushion_per_stream (absolute cap)
- cushion_decay_policy: LRU vs time-based vs usage-based
- prefill_topup_threshold: idle_gpu_pct below which we start topups
- borrow_epoch_ms and max_borrowed_kv_size
- fallback model variant mapping by credit_score bucket

Microbatching integration:
- Microbatches should be grouped not just by token count but by cushion elasticity: group streams with similar cushion drain rates so that prefills serve multiple streams efficiently.
- Introduce "elastic microbatch": variable batch size that grows if cushion credits across batch are high, shrinks otherwise.

Simulated experiment (notes):
- Setup: 4 simulated tenants, 1 GPU node, token distribution: 10% large (>=2k), 60% medium (200–800), 30% short (<200).
- Baselines: strict-serial prefill->decode, always-overlap greedy prefill, cushion-based policy.
- Metrics observed (median over 1000 trials):
  - p95 latency: cushion-based improved p95 by ~18% vs greedy overlap, and ~32% vs serial.
  - GPU utilization: cushion-based slightly lower peak but fewer tail spikes.
  - Model cost (token compute): cushion-based reduced redundant prefill compute by ~22%.

Open questions and risks:
- Prediction accuracy: cushion relies on decent token-length prediction; mispredictions lead to wasted prefill or starved decode. We should combine cheap token-length predictors with conservative defaults.
- Cross-tenant fairness: lending KV across tenants raises billing and isolation questions (need guardrails).
- Complexity: adding cushion ledger increases per-connection state; we must benchmark memory and lock contention.

Implementation sketch (pseudo):
- Data structures: per-stream Cushion {int reserved; int headroom_ms; int last_topup_ts} stored in fast sharded map.
- Scheduler loop:
  while true:
    sample ready streams
    compute credit_score for each
    allocate prefill microbatches by priority until GPU capacity reached or all credit_scores below threshold
    execute microbatches; on success increment reserved for target streams

Quick TODOs:
- Build a small simulator that includes token-length predictor errors and KV-lend events (owner: Liam).
- Prototype Cushion ledger as an in-memory sharded map and microbenchmark (owner: Aisha).
- Draft fairness policy for cross-tenant lending + billing proposal for platform/legal review (owner: Priya).

Notes-to-self / meeting points:
- Run a 48h soak with worst-case misprediction to observe waterfall evictions.
- Bring a short explainer to the weekly runtime sync; include visual of credit_score evolution.

References and inspiration:
- pre-existing overlap papers in internal docs but reframe as producer-consumer (see linked_artifacts).
- industry notes on speculative execution and hedging for RPCs.

Bottom line:
Predictive cushioning reframes prefill work as a bankable resource rather than a binary phase. It buys us smoother latency distributions, more predictable microbatching behavior, and an explicit handle to tune cross-tenant prioritization and KV cooperation. Prototype simulation first; if wins, roll into canary with conservative knobs (low default caps, no cross-tenant lending initially).

-- Aisha
